chunks: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) narrated from Saad ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was saying: 'Indeed, when the servant prolongs his prostration where no one sees him, Satan exclaims: Alas! Woe to me! They obeyed and I disobeyed; they prostrated and I refused.'
ai.seo_question: What does Satan say when a person prostrates in private?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to emphasize the spiritual potency of *sujud al-shukr* or voluntary prostration performed in solitude, where the believer's humility contrasts with Satan's pride. This specific lament underscores the cosmological narrative of Iblis's refusal to prostrate to Adam, framing private worship as a direct counter to his disobedience. The hadith thus serves as both a comfort to the worshipper and a reminder of the ongoing spiritual battle between human obedience and satanic defiance.
